_comment: Overflight default configuration. All values are client-side and cosmetic.
_presetComment: Presets override the sections below. Valid values: realistic (physics as measured, the default), busy (dense modern airspace over Europe), quiet (remote ocean traffic levels), chemtrail (persistent trails forced on, heavy traffic, deliberate crosshatching -- the look, not the physics), coldwar (low-bypass military-heavy mix), abandoned (no traffic at all, for post-apocalyptic worlds), custom (ignore presets, use the values below).

traffic._comment: densityPerHour is flights entering a 1000x1000 km area per hour. Real-world busy European airspace is ~120; empty ocean is ~4.
traffic._scheduleComment: Optional gate for RP and post-apocalyptic worlds: traffic multiplier by in-game day. Empty list = always 1.0.
traffic._mixComment: Relative weights, normalised automatically. Cruise levels in FL (hundreds of feet).

atmosphere._comment: Minecraft has no real atmosphere, so one is synthesised from biome temperature, weather state and a slowly evolving noise field.
atmosphere._issrComment: Ice-supersaturated regions: the patches of sky where trails persist. Frequency is how much of the sky qualifies on an average day.

trails._comment: formationBiasK shifts the Schmidt-Appleman threshold; positive makes trails easier. persistenceMultiplier scales how long surviving trails live.

render._comment: Aircraft and trails are drawn on a fixed-radius celestial shell, never as world entities, so they clip against nothing and cost nothing to tick.
